channel.title: FORTUNA SIGNAL — Briefs
channel.description: Published research briefs from FORTUNA SIGNAL.

item.title: A new kitchen behind a familiar dining room
item.description: A payment can look familiar while the machinery behind it changes. Visa's stablecoin announcement offers a window into that quieter transformation.

item.title: The five questions behind every dossier
item.description: Every token in the Asset Library is read against the same five questions — the FORA-01 verification standard. Here is what they are, and why the order matters.

item.title: How to read a FORTUNA SIGNAL dossier
item.description: Every dossier follows the same contract — a verification chip, a plain-language utility line, five verdicts, and the evidence behind them. Here is the ninety-second read.

item.title: We went looking for 126 whitepapers. 64 tokens didn't have one.
item.description: FORTUNA's research corpus now covers 126 tokens. For 62, we read the official whitepaper. For 64 — including some of the largest names in crypto — no whitepaper exists. A missing primary document is itself a finding.

item.title: More ovens do not guarantee more dinners
item.description: Powerful hardware is only part of the AI story. Follow the work from capacity to paying customers — and then examine where the token fits.

item.title: When the studio shuts down — what happened to Pirate Nation
item.description: Proof of Play, the a16z-backed studio behind Pirate Nation, shut down in August 2026 and open-sourced the game. The PIRATE token persists under an independent foundation — but the game is no longer a live service.

item.title: Redemption is the test
item.description: Four of the five verification questions are about setup. The last two — how redemption works, and who is liable if it fails — are where most token stories actually end.

item.title: The ticket and the treasure
item.description: A coat-check ticket is useful because something stands behind it. Tokenization invites the same question: what makes the digital claim meaningful?

item.title: What "unverified" means here
item.description: UNVERIFIED is a finding, not a shrug. Why this site treats "no evidence found" as a result worth publishing — and what it is not.
